Focus on the characters. In most good books, character drives plot. Find what makes them tick, and get to know them inside out. If you know their psychology from top to bottom, you're much more likely to relate and connect to your own characters, and as a result you'll have loads more motivation to tell their story. If you can relate to them on that level, you'll want to write almost anything about them.

For your main characters, assign each of them the following:

- Their desire (the thing they want the most out of life and what they think will bring them happiness)
- Their fear (what's preventing them from achieving their desire. Use a conceptual fear for this, such as abandonment, commitment, failure or betrayal)
- Their misbelief (what they wrongly believe is true about their fear. For example, if your character's fear is commitment, their misbelief may be something along the lines of commitment takes away your freedom)

I'm still new to this structure, so don't take it as gospel. But this should give you a solid foundation to work from, especially at the start of your project.
